definitions.explanation: A traditional toy consisting of two long poles with footrests, used for walking at an elevated height. Made from bamboo in traditional Japanese style.

examples.japanese: {竹馬|たけうま}に{乗|の}れるようになった。
examples.english: I learned how to walk on stilts.

examples.japanese: {運動会|うんどうかい}で{竹馬|たけうま}{競走|きょうそう}をした。
examples.english: We had a stilt race at the sports day.

examples.japanese: {竹馬|たけうま}の{友|とも}は{幼|おさな}なじみのことだ。
examples.english: 'Childhood stilt friend' means a childhood friend.

notes:
LITERAL MEANING:
・{竹|たけ} (bamboo) + {馬|うま} (horse) = "bamboo horse"
・Traditionally made from bamboo poles
・Modern versions often made from aluminum or plastic

IDIOMS:
・{竹馬|たけうま}の{友|とも} (childhood friend, lit. "stilt friend")
  → Friends from a young age who played together on stilts

TRADITIONAL GAME:
・Popular children's activity in Japan
・Often used at {運動会|うんどうかい} (school sports festivals)
・Requires balance and practice

RELATED TRADITIONAL GAMES:
・お{手玉|てだま} (beanbag juggling)
・けん{玉|だま} (cup-and-ball)
・{独楽|こま} (spinning top)
・{凧揚|たこあ}げ (kite flying)

COLLOCATIONS:
・{竹馬|たけうま}に{乗|の}る (to walk on stilts)
・{竹馬|たけうま}で{歩|ある}く (to walk on stilts)
・{竹馬|たけうま}から{落|お}ちる (to fall from stilts)
